contextBoundaryNote: Pre-1945 events (McMahon–Hussein, Sykes–Picot, Balfour Declaration, and the 1939 White Paper) are background context only; Edexcel Option P5 strictly examines 1945–95.

root.label: Middle East, 1945–95
root.gloss: Fifty years of Arab–Israeli conflict, superpower rivalry, and peace diplomacy from Britain's postwar Mandate crisis to the 1993–95 Oslo Accords.

children.label: KT1: Birth of Israel
children.gloss: Key topic 1: The birth of the state of Israel, 1945–63 — British withdrawal, the 1948–49 Arab–Israeli war and Palestinian Arab refugees, plus Nasser and the 1956 Suez Crisis.

children.label: 1.1 British Withdrawal & Israel
children.q2Chain: Conflicting Mandate demands & Zionist insurgency (1945–47) → UN Resolution 181 partition & British withdrawal → Declaration of Israel & 1948–49 Arab–Israeli War
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Conflicting Mandate demands & Zionist insurgency (1945–47) → UN Resolution 181 partition & British withdrawal → Declaration of Israel & 1948–49 Arab–Israeli War.

children.label: Jewish & Arab Mandate Demands
children.gloss: Conflicting interests and demands of Jews and Arabs within the British Mandate clashed over postwar Holocaust refugee immigration and majority-rule Arab independence.

children.label: 250,000 Holocaust Survivors in Europe
children.detail: Truman urged Britain to grant 100,000 immediate visas so displaced Jews could build a homeland.
children.gloss: Truman urged Britain to grant 100,000 immediate visas so displaced Jews could build a homeland.

children.label: Bevin Enforced 1,500 Monthly Quota
children.detail: Royal Navy patrols intercepted refugee ships so Britain would not alienate oil-rich Arab states.
children.gloss: Royal Navy patrols intercepted refugee ships so Britain would not alienate oil-rich Arab states.

children.label: United Resistance Sabotage Campaign
children.detail: Haganah, Irgun, and Lehi jointly bombed Mandate railways, bridges, and coastal radar stations.
children.gloss: Haganah, Irgun, and Lehi jointly bombed Mandate railways, bridges, and coastal radar stations.

children.label: 100,000 British Soldiers Tied Down
children.detail: Policing Palestine and conducting Operation Agatha mass arrests drained Britain's bankrupt treasury.
children.gloss: Policing Palestine and conducting Operation Agatha mass arrests drained Britain's bankrupt treasury.

children.label: Trapped Britain Between USA & Arabs
children.detail: Arab demands for majority rule clashed with US visa pressure, leaving London no workable compromise.
children.gloss: Arab demands for majority rule clashed with US visa pressure, leaving London no workable compromise.

children.label: King David Hotel Bombing
children.gloss: The bombing of the King David Hotel in Jerusalem on 22 July 1946 destroyed British military and civil headquarters, accelerating the end of the British Mandate.

children.label: Irgun Retaliation for Agatha Raids
children.detail: Menachem Begin's underground militia targeted British headquarters in Jerusalem after mass arrests.
children.gloss: Menachem Begin's underground militia targeted British headquarters in Jerusalem after mass arrests.

children.label: Milk-Can Blast Killed 91 People
children.detail: Explosives hidden in the basement collapsed six floors housing Britain's military and civil offices.
children.gloss: Explosives hidden in the basement collapsed six floors housing Britain's military and civil offices.

children.label: Haganah Broke Off Irgun Alliance
children.detail: Appalled by mass civilian deaths, Ben-Gurion split mainstream Zionist forces from extremist bombers.
children.gloss: Appalled by mass civilian deaths, Ben-Gurion split mainstream Zionist forces from extremist bombers.

children.label: British Public Demanded Troop Exit
children.detail: Heavy casualties shocked MPs and voters in London, wrecking domestic support for staying in Palestine.
children.gloss: Heavy casualties shocked MPs and voters in London, wrecking domestic support for staying in Palestine.

children.label: Proved Mandate Was Ungovernable
children.detail: Destroying Britain's command centre showed 100,000 troops could not defeat the insurgency by force.
children.gloss: Destroying Britain's command centre showed 100,000 troops could not defeat the insurgency by force.

children.label: Sergeants Affair & SS Exodus
children.gloss: In July 1947 the Sergeants Affair and Royal Navy interception of SS Exodus destroyed British domestic and international support for keeping the Mandate.

children.label: Irgun Hanged Two British Sergeants
children.detail: After three Irgun fighters were executed, militants abducted two army sergeants and mined their bodies.
children.gloss: After three Irgun fighters were executed, militants abducted two army sergeants and mined their bodies.

children.label: Outrage & Riots Across British Cities
children.detail: Front-page photos of the hanged soldiers united press and Parliament behind quitting the Mandate.
children.gloss: Front-page photos of the hanged soldiers united press and Parliament behind quitting the Mandate.

children.label: SS Exodus Survivors Sent to Germany
children.detail: Forcing 4,500 Holocaust refugees back to camps in British-run Germany ruined London's moral standing.
children.gloss: Forcing 4,500 Holocaust refugees back to camps in British-run Germany ruined London's moral standing.

children.label: Sealed Britain's Withdrawal Decision
children.detail: Watched first-hand by UN investigators, these twin crises boosted global backing for partition.
children.gloss: Watched first-hand by UN investigators, these twin crises boosted global backing for partition.

children.label: UN Resolution 181 & Partition
children.gloss: After Britain referred the Mandate to the UN, UN Resolution 181 approved partition into Jewish and Arab states, leading directly to the creation of Israel.

children.label: Bankrupt Britain Handed Issue to UN
children.detail: Exhausted after World War Two, London asked the United Nations in February 1947 to decide Palestine.
children.gloss: Exhausted after World War Two, London asked the United Nations in February 1947 to decide Palestine.

children.label: Nov 1947 Vote to Partition Palestine
children.detail: Resolution 181 gave 55% of the land to a Jewish state and placed Jerusalem under international rule.
children.gloss: Resolution 181 gave 55% of the land to a Jewish state and placed Jerusalem under international rule.

children.label: Arab Rejection Sparked Civil War
children.detail: Jewish leaders accepted partition, while Palestinian Arabs fought losing half the country despite a majority.
children.gloss: Jewish leaders accepted partition, while Palestinian Arabs fought losing half the country despite a majority.

children.label: Israel Proclaimed on 14 May 1948
children.detail: Hours before British rule expired, Ben-Gurion declared independence and won rapid US-Soviet backing.
children.gloss: Hours before British rule expired, Ben-Gurion declared independence and won rapid US-Soviet backing.

children.label: Gave Legal Legitimacy for Statehood
children.detail: Rare joint voting by Washington and Moscow anchored Israel in international law from day one.
children.gloss: Rare joint voting by Washington and Moscow anchored Israel in international law from day one.

children.label: 1948–49 Arab–Israeli War
children.gloss: Key events of the Arab-Israeli war (1948–49) saw five Arab League states invade on 15 May 1948 before Israeli reorganization and Czech arms secured victory.

children.label: Five Divided Arab Armies Invaded
children.detail: Egypt, Syria, Jordan, Iraq, and Lebanon attacked on 15 May 1948, but rival war aims split their command.
children.gloss: Egypt, Syria, Jordan, Iraq, and Lebanon attacked on 15 May 1948, but rival war aims split their command.

children.label: June UN Truce & Czech Arms Airlift
children.detail: During a four-week ceasefire, Israel unified its army and imported vital Czech weapons and aircraft.
children.gloss: During a four-week ceasefire, Israel unified its army and imported vital Czech weapons and aircraft.

children.label: IDF Offensives Won Galilee & Negev
children.detail: Better-supplied Israeli brigades drove back Egyptian and Syrian troops while Jordan held the Old City.
children.gloss: Better-supplied Israeli brigades drove back Egyptian and Syrian troops while Jordan held the Old City.

children.label: 1949 Rhodes Armistice Agreements
children.detail: Separate UN-mediated truces ended fighting with four neighbours, yet every Arab state refused peace.
children.gloss: Separate UN-mediated truces ended fighting with four neighbours, yet every Arab state refused peace.

children.label: Secured Survival Without Recognition
children.detail: Victory saved the newborn Jewish state, but truce lines without treaties locked in decades of enmity.
children.gloss: Victory saved the newborn Jewish state, but truce lines without treaties locked in decades of enmity.

children.label: 1.2 Aftermath of 1948–49 War
children.q2Chain: 1949 Rhodes Green Line armistice & 700,000 refugees → IDF formation, 1950 Law of Return & US aid → Unresolved border raids & Egyptian hostility
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: 1949 Rhodes Green Line armistice & 700,000 refugees → IDF formation, 1950 Law of Return & US aid → Unresolved border raids & Egyptian hostility.

children.label: Territorial Changes (Green Line)
children.gloss: Territorial changes and their impact under the 1949 Green Line armistices left Israel holding 78% of Mandatory Palestine while Jordan and Egypt held the rest.

children.label: Israel Expanded to 78% of Mandate
children.detail: Ceasefire maps gave Israel 23% more territory than the 1947 UN partition plan had originally offered.
children.gloss: Ceasefire maps gave Israel 23% more territory than the 1947 UN partition plan had originally offered.

children.label: Jordan Held West Bank & Old City
children.detail: Barbed wire divided Jerusalem as Israel governed the western half and Jordan annexed the eastern side.
children.gloss: Barbed wire divided Jerusalem as Israel governed the western half and Jordan annexed the eastern side.

children.label: Proposed Arab State Never Emerged
children.detail: Egypt ran crowded Gaza under military rule without citizenship, leaving Palestinians with no country.
children.gloss: Egypt ran crowded Gaza under military rule without citizenship, leaving Palestinians with no country.

children.label: Vulnerable Borders Invited Clashes
children.detail: Left just nine miles wide near the West Bank, Israel answered cross-border infiltration with tough raids.
children.gloss: Left just nine miles wide near the West Bank, Israel answered cross-border infiltration with tough raids.

children.label: Palestinian Arab Refugees
children.gloss: The refugee status of Palestinian Arabs saw over 700,000 displaced in the Nakba into camps across Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria.

children.label: Deir Yassin Panic & Village Flight
children.detail: Fears after the April 1948 massacre and IDF advances emptied over 400 Palestinian Arab villages.
children.gloss: Fears after the April 1948 massacre and IDF advances emptied over 400 Palestinian Arab villages.

children.label: 700,000 Refugees in UNRWA Camps
children.detail: Displaced families crowded into tent settlements in Gaza, Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria on UN rations.
children.gloss: Displaced families crowded into tent settlements in Gaza, Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria on UN rations.

children.label: Israel Blocked Right of Return
children.detail: Defying UN calls for repatriation, Israeli leaders seized empty homes to protect a Jewish majority.
children.gloss: Defying UN calls for repatriation, Israeli leaders seized empty homes to protect a Jewish majority.

children.label: Permanent Exile Fuelled Fedayeen
children.detail: Known to Palestinians as the Nakba, camp statelessness drove youths to join armed border fighters.
children.gloss: Known to Palestinians as the Nakba, camp statelessness drove youths to join armed border fighters.

children.label: IDF & Law of Return (1950)
children.gloss: Creation of the Israeli Defence Forces and the 1950 Law of Return doubled Israel’s population, while US aid to Israel kept the young state solvent.

children.label: Militias Unified Into Conscript IDF
children.detail: Compulsory military service and trained civilian reserves let outnumbered Israel mobilise within 48 hours.
children.gloss: Compulsory military service and trained civilian reserves let outnumbered Israel mobilise within 48 hours.

children.label: Jewish Population Doubled by 1952
children.detail: Granting every Jew automatic citizenship brought survivors from Europe and Arab states to 1.4 million.
children.gloss: Granting every Jew automatic citizenship brought survivors from Europe and Arab states to 1.4 million.

children.label: Austerity Eased by $100m US Loans
children.detail: Housing hundreds of thousands of newcomers forced food rationing until American credit funded new towns.
children.gloss: Housing hundreds of thousands of newcomers forced food rationing until American credit funded new towns.

children.label: Built Lasting Military & US Lifeline
children.detail: Rapid immigration populated frontier settlements, expanded army reserves, and tied survival to US aid.
children.gloss: Rapid immigration populated frontier settlements, expanded army reserves, and tied survival to US aid.

children.label: US Aid & Relations with Egypt
children.gloss: US aid to Israel strengthened the new state economically while Israel’s relations with Egypt deteriorated over Suez blockades and Gaza border raids.

children.label: 1948 Defeat Sparked Cairo Coup
children.detail: Humiliation in Palestine helped army officers topple Egypt's king in 1952 and harden hostility to Israel.
children.gloss: Humiliation in Palestine helped army officers topple Egypt's king in 1952 and harden hostility to Israel.

children.label: Egypt Choked Suez & Tiran Shipping
children.detail: Cairo barred Israeli cargo from the canal and blockaded Eilat, throttling southern oil and Asian trade.
children.gloss: Cairo barred Israeli cargo from the canal and blockaded Eilat, throttling southern oil and Asian trade.

children.label: Gaza Fedayeen Raids & IDF Strikes
children.detail: Palestinian guerrilla attacks from Egyptian-held territory triggered fierce Israeli army reprisals.
children.gloss: Palestinian guerrilla attacks from Egyptian-held territory triggered fierce Israeli army reprisals.

children.label: Made Egypt Israel's Chief Rival
children.detail: Sea blockades and deadly Gaza border clashes pushed Cairo and Tel Aviv steadily toward war by 1956.
children.gloss: Sea blockades and deadly Gaza border clashes pushed Cairo and Tel Aviv steadily toward war by 1956.

children.label: 1.3 Increased Tension, 1955–63
children.q2Chain: Nasser's rise & Israel's 1955 Gaza raid → Czech arms deal & July 1956 Suez Canal nationalisation → Sèvres plot, Suez Crisis & 1958 UAR
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Nasser's rise & Israel's 1955 Gaza raid → Czech arms deal & July 1956 Suez Canal nationalisation → Sèvres plot, Suez Crisis & 1958 UAR.

children.label: Nasser & Arab World Leadership
children.gloss: Gamal Abdel Nasser asserted Egypt’s leadership of the Arab world through Pan-Arab nationalism, neutralism, and defiance of Western Cold War pacts.

children.label: Nasser's Pan-Arab Nationalist Appeal
children.detail: Cairo radio rallied millions across the region to throw off British bases and unite against Israel.
children.gloss: Cairo radio rallied millions across the region to throw off British bases and unite against Israel.

children.label: Rejected Pro-Western Baghdad Pact
children.detail: Championing non-aligned Arab independence angered Britain and pushed Washington to pull Aswan Dam loans.
children.gloss: Championing non-aligned Arab independence angered Britain and pushed Washington to pull Aswan Dam loans.

children.label: Sept 1955 Czech-Soviet Arms Deal
children.detail: Trading Egyptian cotton for Soviet jets and tanks broke Western arms limits and alarmed Israeli planners.
children.gloss: Trading Egyptian cotton for Soviet jets and tanks broke Western arms limits and alarmed Israeli planners.

children.label: Pulled Cold War Rivalry Into Region
children.detail: Turning to Moscow for modern weapons made the USSR a key Arab patron against Western-backed rivals.
children.gloss: Turning to Moscow for modern weapons made the USSR a key Arab patron against Western-backed rivals.

children.label: Attacks on Gaza (1955) & Sinai
children.gloss: Events and significance of Israeli attacks on Gaza in February 1955 and Sinai in October 1956 humiliated Egypt’s army and triggered open war.

children.label: Feb 1955 Gaza Raid Killed 38 Troops
children.detail: Israeli paratroopers struck an Egyptian army camp after border infiltrations, exposing Cairo's weakness.
children.gloss: Israeli paratroopers struck an Egyptian army camp after border infiltrations, exposing Cairo's weakness.

children.label: Oct 1956 IDF Sweep Across Sinai
children.detail: Moshe Dayan's paratroopers and tanks overran Gaza bases and reached Sharm el-Sheikh within days.
children.gloss: Moshe Dayan's paratroopers and tanks overran Gaza bases and reached Sharm el-Sheikh within days.

children.label: Gaza Shock Drove Arms & Blockade
children.detail: Stung by the 1955 raid, Nasser bought Soviet weapons, stepped up fedayeen attacks, and shut Tiran.
children.gloss: Stung by the 1955 raid, Nasser bought Soviet weapons, stepped up fedayeen attacks, and shut Tiran.

children.label: UNEF Buffer Reopened Tiran Shipping
children.detail: Israel withdrew from Sinai in 1957 once UN peacekeepers guarded the border and Eilat sea lanes opened.
children.gloss: Israel withdrew from Sinai in 1957 once UN peacekeepers guarded the border and Eilat sea lanes opened.

children.label: Proved IDF Speed & Won 10-Year Calm
children.detail: Victory crushed Gaza guerrilla bases and kept Egypt's southern border quiet until Nasser gambled in 1967.
children.gloss: Victory crushed Gaza guerrilla bases and kept Egypt's southern border quiet until Nasser gambled in 1967.

children.label: Suez Crisis (1956) & UAR (1958)
children.gloss: Events and significance of the Suez Crisis (1956), including the formation of the UAR in 1958, ended Anglo-French dominance and elevated Nasser.

children.label: Nasser Nationalised the Suez Canal
children.detail: After America cancelled Aswan High Dam funding in July 1956, Cairo seized canal tolls to pay for it.
children.gloss: After America cancelled Aswan High Dam funding in July 1956, Cairo seized canal tolls to pay for it.

children.label: Secret Protocol of Sèvres Collusion
children.detail: Britain, France, and Israel plotted an IDF Sinai strike as an excuse for Anglo-French troops to land.
children.gloss: Britain, France, and Israel plotted an IDF Sinai strike as an excuse for Anglo-French troops to land.

children.label: Eisenhower Forced UK-French Retreat
children.detail: Threatening Britain's currency and loans, US pressure forced a humiliating ceasefire and Eden's exit.
children.gloss: Threatening Britain's currency and loans, US pressure forced a humiliating ceasefire and Eden's exit.

children.label: Egypt & Syria Merged Into 1958 UAR
children.detail: Keeping the canal made Nasser an Arab hero, inspiring a three-year political union under Cairo's rule.
children.gloss: Keeping the canal made Nasser an Arab hero, inspiring a three-year political union under Cairo's rule.

children.label: Superpowers Replaced UK & France
children.detail: Anglo-French imperial clout collapsed, leaving Washington and Moscow competing to dominate the region.
children.gloss: Anglo-French imperial clout collapsed, leaving Washington and Moscow competing to dominate the region.

children.label: KT2: Escalating Conflict
children.gloss: Key topic 2: The escalating conflict, 1964–73 — the 1964 Cairo Conference, 1967 Six-Day War, UN Resolution 242, occupied territories, PLO terrorism, and the 1973 Yom Kippur War.

children.label: 2.1 The Six-Day War, 1967
children.q2Chain: 1964 Cairo Conference, PLO, Syrian-backed Fatah raids, Samu & 7 April → May 1967 Soviet report, UNEF expelled & Tiran closed → Operation Focus & Six-Day Israeli victory
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: 1964 Cairo Conference, PLO, Syrian-backed Fatah raids, Samu & 7 April → May 1967 Soviet report, UNEF expelled & Tiran closed → Operation Focus & Six-Day Israeli victory.

children.label: Cairo Conference (1964) & PLO
children.gloss: The Cairo Conference (1964) united Arab leaders against Israel’s National Water Carrier, backed headwater diversion, and created the PLO.

children.label: Dispute Over Jordan River Water
children.detail: Israel's new pipeline pumping Galilee water south to the Negev prompted Arab plans to divert headwaters.
children.gloss: Israel's new pipeline pumping Galilee water south to the Negev prompted Arab plans to divert headwaters.

children.label: PLO Founded in May 1964
children.detail: Summit leaders backed a formal Palestinian political body whose charter rejected Israel's right to exist.
children.gloss: Summit leaders backed a formal Palestinian political body whose charter rejected Israel's right to exist.

children.label: Unified Arab Military Command Set Up
children.detail: Nasser delayed premature war, yet joint defence pledges tied his prestige to protecting militant Syria.
children.gloss: Nasser delayed premature war, yet joint defence pledges tied his prestige to protecting militant Syria.

children.label: Gave Voice Yet Spurred Rival Fatah
children.detail: Egyptian control over the early PLO frustrated Yasser Arafat, whose fighters began raids in January 1965.
children.gloss: Egyptian control over the early PLO frustrated Yasser Arafat, whose fighters began raids in January 1965.

children.label: Syria, Fatah, Samu & 7 April
children.gloss: Escalating tension between Israel, Syria and Jordan grew through Syria’s support for Fatah, Israel’s raid on Samu, and the air battle of 7 April 1967.

children.label: Syria Sheltered Fatah Guerrillas
children.detail: Damascus armed Arafat's saboteurs and shelled northern farms from the Golan Heights to drag Arabs to war.
children.gloss: Damascus armed Arafat's saboteurs and shelled northern farms from the Golan Heights to drag Arabs to war.

children.label: Nov 1966 IDF Raid on Samu Village
children.detail: After a landmine killed three Israelis, tanks flattened West Bank homes and killed Jordanian soldiers.
children.gloss: After a landmine killed three Israelis, tanks flattened West Bank homes and killed Jordanian soldiers.

children.label: Six Syrian MiGs Downed (7 Apr 1967)
children.detail: Border clashes escalated into an aerial dogfight that publicly humiliated Damascus's Soviet-armed air force.
children.gloss: Border clashes escalated into an aerial dogfight that publicly humiliated Damascus's Soviet-armed air force.

children.label: Panic Activated Cairo-Syria Pact
children.detail: Fearing a full Israeli assault after losing six jets, Syrian leaders begged Moscow and Nasser to step in.
children.gloss: Fearing a full Israeli assault after losing six jets, Syrian leaders begged Moscow and Nasser to step in.

children.label: Pushed Hussein & Nasser Toward War
children.detail: West Bank riots after Samu forced moderate Jordan to align with Egypt when crisis erupted in May 1967.
children.gloss: West Bank riots after Samu forced moderate Jordan to align with Egypt when crisis erupted in May 1967.

children.label: USSR, Nasser & USA Before War
children.gloss: Actions of the USSR, Nasser and the USA in May 1967 escalated from a false Soviet intelligence warning to closing the Straits of Tiran.

children.label: False Soviet Invasion Warning (May)
children.detail: Moscow wrongly told Cairo that Israeli brigades were massing against Syria, daring Nasser to respond.
children.gloss: Moscow wrongly told Cairo that Israeli brigades were massing against Syria, daring Nasser to respond.

children.label: UNEF Expelled & Tiran Closed (May)
children.detail: Nasser marched 100,000 troops into Sinai, removed UN peacekeepers, and blocked Eilat shipping lanes.
children.gloss: Nasser marched 100,000 troops into Sinai, removed UN peacekeepers, and blocked Eilat shipping lanes.

children.label: Jordan Joined Egypt's Defence Pact
children.detail: King Hussein placed his army under Egyptian command on 30 May while US naval diplomacy stalled.
children.gloss: King Hussein placed his army under Egyptian command on 30 May while US naval diplomacy stalled.

children.label: Moshe Dayan Named Defence Minister
children.detail: Encircled on three borders, Israel formed a unity cabinet ready to strike before Arab armies attacked.
children.gloss: Encircled on three borders, Israel formed a unity cabinet ready to strike before Arab armies attacked.

children.label: Made Pre-Emptive Strike Inevitable
children.detail: Closing Eilat crossed Israel's 1957 red line while hesitant Washington failed to reopen the waterway.
children.gloss: Closing Eilat crossed Israel's 1957 red line while hesitant Washington failed to reopen the waterway.

children.label: Six-Day War Key Events
children.gloss: Key events of the Six-Day War saw Operation Focus wipe out Arab air forces on 5 June before Israel seized Sinai, East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and Golan.

children.label: 5 June Air Strike Destroyed 300+ Jets
children.detail: Flying low under radar in Operation Focus, Israel wiped out Egypt's grounded bombers within three hours.
children.gloss: Flying low under radar in Operation Focus, Israel wiped out Egypt's grounded bombers within three hours.

children.label: Sinai, Gaza & Old City Captured
children.detail: Unchallenged from the sky, IDF tanks reached Suez and paratroopers took East Jerusalem and the West Bank.
children.gloss: Unchallenged from the sky, IDF tanks reached Suez and paratroopers took East Jerusalem and the West Bank.

children.label: Golan Heights Stormed (9–10 June)
children.detail: Infantry and armoured bulldozers overran fortified Syrian ridges, ending artillery fire on Galilee farms.
children.gloss: Infantry and armoured bulldozers overran fortified Syrian ridges, ending artillery fire on Galilee farms.

children.label: Tripled Territory & Crushed Prestige
children.detail: Routing three Arab states won deep defensive buffers, strengthened US ties, and humbled Pan-Arabism.
children.gloss: Routing three Arab states won deep defensive buffers, strengthened US ties, and humbled Pan-Arabism.

children.label: 2.2 Aftermath of 1967 War
children.q2Chain: Five occupied territories, Khartoum 'Three Noes' & UN Resolution 242 → 1970 PFLP hijackings & Black September PLO expulsion from Jordan → 1972 Munich Olympics massacre & Israeli retaliation
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Five occupied territories, Khartoum 'Three Noes' & UN Resolution 242 → 1970 PFLP hijackings & Black September PLO expulsion from Jordan → 1972 Munich Olympics massacre & Israeli retaliation.

children.label: UN Resolution 242 & Suez Canal
children.gloss: UN Resolution 242 established the Land for Peace formula amid the Khartoum deadlock and continued dispute over the blocked Suez Canal.

children.label: Khartoum Summit 'Three Noes' (1967)
children.detail: Defeated Arab leaders vowed no peace, no recognition, and no direct negotiations, hardening deadlock.
children.gloss: Defeated Arab leaders vowed no peace, no recognition, and no direct negotiations, hardening deadlock.

children.label: UN Resolution 242 'Land for Peace'
children.detail: Ambiguous wording traded Israeli withdrawal from occupied land for Arab recognition of secure borders.
children.gloss: Ambiguous wording traded Israeli withdrawal from occupied land for Arab recognition of secure borders.

children.label: PLO Angered by 'Refugee' Wording
children.detail: Because 242 omitted an independent Palestinian state, Arafat's movement rejected the text until 1988.
children.gloss: Because 242 omitted an independent Palestinian state, Arafat's movement rejected the text until 1988.

children.label: Blocked Suez Canal & Bar-Lev Line
children.detail: Sunken ships shut the waterway for eight years as Israel fortified the eastern bank against Egyptian guns.
children.gloss: Sunken ships shut the waterway for eight years as Israel fortified the eastern bank against Egyptian guns.

children.label: Became Blueprint for Later Treaties
children.detail: Despite rival readings, exchanging 1967 territory for diplomatic peace underpinned Camp David and Oslo.
children.gloss: Despite rival readings, exchanging 1967 territory for diplomatic peace underpinned Camp David and Oslo.

children.label: Refugees & 5 Occupied Lands
children.gloss: New Palestinian refugees fled as Israel held five occupied territories: the Golan Heights, Gaza Strip, West Bank, Sinai, and East Jerusalem.

children.label: Five Strategic Regions Under IDF
children.detail: Israel held Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, the Golan Heights, and annexed East Jerusalem into its capital.
children.gloss: Israel held Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, the Golan Heights, and annexed East Jerusalem into its capital.

children.label: 300,000 More Refugees Fled East
children.detail: Families displaced a second time since 1948 packed Jordanian camps and swelled guerrilla recruitment.
children.gloss: Families displaced a second time since 1948 packed Jordanian camps and swelled guerrilla recruitment.

children.label: One Million Palestinians Ruled by IDF
children.detail: Military governors enforced curfews, travel permits, and land seizures across Gaza and the West Bank.
children.gloss: Military governors enforced curfews, travel permits, and land seizures across Gaza and the West Bank.

children.label: Shifted Conflict to Daily Occupation
children.detail: Captured land offered bargaining chips with Arab states, yet ruling a captive population bred revolt.
children.gloss: Captured land offered bargaining chips with Arab states, yet ruling a captive population bred revolt.

children.label: PFLP Hijacks & Jordan Expulsion
children.gloss: The PFLP airplane hijacks of 1970 defied King Hussein, triggering the Black September civil war and the expulsion of the PLO from Jordan (1970–71).

children.label: PLO 'State-Within-a-State' in Jordan
children.detail: Armed fighters manned Amman checkpoints and launched raids that threatened King Hussein's royal rule.
children.gloss: Armed fighters manned Amman checkpoints and launched raids that threatened King Hussein's royal rule.

children.label: Dawson's Field Hijackings (Sept 1970)
children.detail: Radical PFLP militants seized four Western airliners and blew up three empty jets before TV cameras.
children.gloss: Radical PFLP militants seized four Western airliners and blew up three empty jets before TV cameras.

children.label: Black September Army Crackdown
children.detail: Hussein's loyal forces shelled refugee camps in Amman while US-Israeli warnings deterred Syrian tanks.
children.gloss: Hussein's loyal forces shelled refugee camps in Amman while US-Israeli warnings deterred Syrian tanks.

children.label: PLO Driven Out to Beirut (1970–71)
children.detail: Expelled from Jordan, Arafat moved guerrilla headquarters into fragile, divided southern Lebanon.
children.searchTerm: expulsion of the PLO from Jordan
children.gloss: Expelled from Jordan, Arafat moved guerrilla headquarters into fragile, divided southern Lebanon.

children.label: Fractured Arabs & Bred Terror Cells
children.detail: Losing Jordan's long border split Arab states and spawned covert extremists seeking global headlines.
children.gloss: Losing Jordan's long border split Arab states and spawned covert extremists seeking global headlines.

children.label: Munich Olympics & Response
children.gloss: Use of terrorism at the 1972 Munich Olympics by Black September triggered fierce Israeli retaliation and polarized international attitudes towards the Palestine issue.

children.label: 11 Israeli Olympians Killed (1972)
children.detail: Black September gunmen seized athletes in Munich; all hostages died after a botched airfield rescue.
children.gloss: Black September gunmen seized athletes in Munich; all hostages died after a botched airfield rescue.

children.label: Meir Ordered Bombings & Mossad Hits
children.detail: Israeli jets pounded Lebanese camps while covert intelligence squads hunted terror planners in Europe.
children.gloss: Israeli jets pounded Lebanese camps while covert intelligence squads hunted terror planners in Europe.

children.label: Western Nations Boycotted the PLO
children.detail: Televised murder of athletes entrenched the terrorist label and hardened US-Israeli refusal to talk.
children.gloss: Televised murder of athletes entrenched the terrorist label and hardened US-Israeli refusal to talk.

children.label: Forced Palestine Into Global Focus
children.detail: Watched by 900 million viewers, shock publicity tarnished militants yet pushed Arafat toward UN talks.
children.gloss: Watched by 900 million viewers, shock publicity tarnished militants yet pushed Arafat toward UN talks.

children.label: 2.3 Israel & Egypt, 1967–73
children.q2Chain: War of Attrition (1969–70) & Israeli settlement consolidation → Sadat's rejected 1971 peace offer & 1972 expulsion of Soviet advisers → October 1973 Yom Kippur War, superpower airlifts & UN Resolution 338
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: War of Attrition (1969–70) & Israeli settlement consolidation → Sadat's rejected 1971 peace offer & 1972 expulsion of Soviet advisers → October 1973 Yom Kippur War, superpower airlifts & UN Resolution 338.

children.label: Egypt's Ties: US, USSR & Arabs
children.gloss: Egyptian relations with Israel, the USA, the USSR and other Arab states shifted from Nasser’s War of Attrition to Sadat expelling Soviet advisers and aligning with Syria.

children.label: War of Attrition Along Suez (1969–70)
children.detail: Heavy Egyptian shelling tried to break Israel's canal forts, pulling in Soviet missiles until a truce.
children.gloss: Heavy Egyptian shelling tried to break Israel's canal forts, pulling in Soviet missiles until a truce.

children.label: Sadat's 1971 Canal Offer Ignored
children.detail: Egypt's new president offered to reopen Suez for partial Sinai pullback, but Israel and America balked.
children.gloss: Egypt's new president offered to reopen Suez for partial Sinai pullback, but Israel and America balked.

children.label: 15,000 Soviet Advisers Expelled (1972)
children.detail: Angered by Moscow holding back offensive arms during détente, Sadat forged a secret war pact with Syria.
children.gloss: Angered by Moscow holding back offensive arms during détente, Sadat forged a secret war pact with Syria.

children.label: Prepared Limited War to Force Talks
children.detail: Ousting Russians signalled openness to Washington while Arab oil states funded October 1973 war plans.
children.gloss: Ousting Russians signalled openness to Washington while Arab oil states funded October 1973 war plans.

children.label: Consolidating Occupied Lands
children.gloss: Israel’s consolidation of control of the occupied territories built perimeter military defences, annexed East Jerusalem, and planted permanent Jewish settlements.

children.label: Drive for Strategic Security Buffers
children.detail: Israeli leaders vowed never to return to narrow pre-1967 borders exposed to Arab tank or gun attacks.
children.gloss: Israeli leaders vowed never to return to narrow pre-1967 borders exposed to Arab tank or gun attacks.

children.label: Jewish Settlements Built in 4 Lands
children.detail: State-funded civilian outposts across the West Bank, Golan, Gaza, and Sinai made pullback harder.
children.gloss: State-funded civilian outposts across the West Bank, Golan, Gaza, and Sinai made pullback harder.

children.label: Bar-Lev Forts Bred IDF Complacency
children.detail: Overconfidence in Sinai sand ramparts led Israeli intelligence to dismiss Arab troop moves in 1973.
children.gloss: Overconfidence in Sinai sand ramparts led Israeli intelligence to dismiss Arab troop moves in 1973.

children.label: Convinced Egypt & Syria to Attack
children.detail: Watching permanent settlements expand persuaded Sadat that waiting meant losing captured land forever.
children.gloss: Watching permanent settlements expand persuaded Sadat that waiting meant losing captured land forever.

children.label: Yom Kippur War & Aftermath
children.gloss: Key events of the Yom Kippur War (1973) and its aftermath moved from surprise Egyptian-Syrian breakthroughs to superpower airlifts and UN Resolution 338.

children.label: 6 Oct Surprise Crossing & Golan Surge
children.detail: Water cannons breached canal sand walls under Soviet SAM cover while Syrian armour stormed the Golan.
children.gloss: Water cannons breached canal sand walls under Soviet SAM cover while Syrian armour stormed the Golan.

children.label: US Airlift & IDF Counter-Attack
children.detail: Emergency American weapons enabled Israeli tanks to push Syria back and trap Egypt's Third Army.
children.gloss: Emergency American weapons enabled Israeli tanks to push Syria back and trap Egypt's Third Army.

children.label: Nuclear Alert & UN Resolution 338
children.detail: Soviet threats to rescue Cairo triggered a US nuclear alert before both superpowers forced a ceasefire.
children.gloss: Soviet threats to rescue Cairo triggered a US nuclear alert before both superpowers forced a ceasefire.

children.label: Heavy Losses Ended Invincibility Myth
children.detail: Over 2,500 Israeli dead shocked the public, sparked an official inquiry, and made Golda Meir resign.
children.gloss: Over 2,500 Israeli dead shocked the public, sparked an official inquiry, and made Golda Meir resign.

children.label: Restored Pride & Unlocked Diplomacy
children.detail: Crossing Suez erased 1967 humiliation for Sadat and proved Israel needed negotiated peace for safety.
children.gloss: Crossing Suez erased 1967 humiliation for Sadat and proved Israel needed negotiated peace for safety.

children.label: KT3: Attempts at a Solution
children.gloss: Key topic 3: Attempts at a solution, 1974–95 — the oil crisis, shuttle diplomacy, Camp David and the 1979 peace treaty, Lebanon, the First Intifada, and the 1993–95 Oslo Accords.

children.label: 3.1 Diplomatic Negotiations
children.q2Chain: 1973–74 OPEC oil crisis & Kissinger's shuttle diplomacy (Suez reopened 1975) → Sadat's 1977 Jerusalem visit & Begin's Ismailia return → 1978 Camp David Accords & 1979 Treaty of Washington
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: 1973–74 OPEC oil crisis & Kissinger's shuttle diplomacy (Suez reopened 1975) → Sadat's 1977 Jerusalem visit & Begin's Ismailia return → 1978 Camp David Accords & 1979 Treaty of Washington.

children.label: 1973 Oil Crisis, USA & USSR
children.gloss: The 1973–74 oil crisis and the involvement of the USA and the USSR reshaped Western energy security and pushed Washington to sideline Moscow.

children.label: OPEC Oil Embargo Punished US Aid
children.detail: Arab oil ministers slashed output and banned sales to America for resupplying Israel in October 1973.
children.gloss: Arab oil ministers slashed output and banned sales to America for resupplying Israel in October 1973.

children.label: Crude Prices Quadrupled Worldwide
children.detail: Fourfold fuel hikes caused Western petrol queues, inflation, and European calls for Palestinian rights.
children.gloss: Fourfold fuel hikes caused Western petrol queues, inflation, and European calls for Palestinian rights.

children.label: Washington Sidelined Soviet Diplomats
children.detail: Because only America held influence over Israel, Sadat turned away from Moscow to deal with Washington.
children.gloss: Because only America held influence over Israel, Sadat turned away from Moscow to deal with Washington.

children.label: Made Peace an Urgent US Priority
children.detail: Economic damage forced American leaders to broker Sinai pullbacks so Arab states lifted the ban in 1974.
children.gloss: Economic damage forced American leaders to broker Sinai pullbacks so Arab states lifted the ban in 1974.

children.label: Kissinger, Shuttle & Suez Canal
children.gloss: Henry Kissinger used step-by-step shuttle diplomacy to broker Sinai I, Golan, and Sinai II pullbacks, securing the reopening of the Suez Canal.

children.label: Step-by-Step Shuttle Flights (1974–75)
children.detail: Kissinger flew repeatedly between Cairo, Tel Aviv, and Damascus to broker Sinai and Golan pullbacks.
children.gloss: Kissinger flew repeatedly between Cairo, Tel Aviv, and Damascus to broker Sinai and Golan pullbacks.

children.label: Suez Canal Reopened in June 1975
children.detail: Israeli troop withdrawal let Egypt clear mines and wrecks, restoring vital shipping tolls after 8 years.
children.gloss: Israeli troop withdrawal let Egypt clear mines and wrecks, restoring vital shipping tolls after 8 years.

children.label: US Aid Pulled Egypt Out of USSR Camp
children.detail: Billions in American economic support and Sinai monitors cemented Cairo's switch to Western alignment.
children.gloss: Billions in American economic support and Sinai monitors cemented Cairo's switch to Western alignment.

children.label: Built Trust Yet Sidelined the PLO
children.detail: Gradual buffer deals paved the way for Camp David, while Kissinger barred US-PLO talks without 242.
children.gloss: Gradual buffer deals paved the way for Camp David, while Kissinger barred US-PLO talks without 242.

children.label: Sadat & Begin Visits (1977)
children.gloss: Sadat’s visit to Israel (November 1977) and Begin’s visit to Egypt (December 1977) shattered thirty years of diplomatic taboo between Israel and an Arab state.

children.label: Egyptian Bread Riots & Economic Need
children.detail: Crushing military budgets sparked 1977 food protests, convincing Sadat Egypt needed peace and US aid.
children.gloss: Crushing military budgets sparked 1977 food protests, convincing Sadat Egypt needed peace and US aid.

children.label: Sadat in Jerusalem & Begin in Egypt
children.detail: Sadat addressed Israel's Knesset in November 1977 before Begin flew to Ismailia for Christmas talks.
children.gloss: Sadat addressed Israel's Knesset in November 1977 before Begin flew to Ismailia for Christmas talks.

children.label: Shattered 30-Year Recognition Taboo
children.detail: Standing inside Israel's parliament overturned Khartoum's Three Noes and won over doubtful Israelis.
children.gloss: Standing inside Israel's parliament overturned Khartoum's Three Noes and won over doubtful Israelis.

children.label: Talks Stalled Over Palestinian Rule
children.detail: Begin resisted uprooting Sinai settlers and refused full independence for Gaza and the West Bank.
children.gloss: Begin resisted uprooting Sinai settlers and refused full independence for Gaza and the West Bank.

children.label: Created Momentum Rescued by Carter
children.detail: Direct leader-to-leader contact opened a historic bilateral path that President Carter saved in 1978.
children.gloss: Direct leader-to-leader contact opened a historic bilateral path that President Carter saved in 1978.

children.label: Carter, Camp David & 1979 Treaty
children.gloss: US President Carter mediated the Camp David Accords (1978) and the Treaty of Washington (1979), forging the first formal Arab–Israeli peace treaty.

children.label: 13-Day Camp David Summit (Sept 1978)
children.detail: President Carter secluded Sadat and Begin in Maryland, pairing Sinai return with vague autonomy plans.
children.gloss: President Carter secluded Sadat and Begin in Maryland, pairing Sinai return with vague autonomy plans.

children.label: Treaty of Washington (March 1979)
children.detail: Israel returned all of Sinai for embassies, canal access, and multi-billion-dollar annual US aid.
children.gloss: Israel returned all of Sinai for embassies, canal access, and multi-billion-dollar annual US aid.

children.label: Egypt Suspended & Sadat Assassinated
children.detail: Furious Arab states boycotted Cairo for a separate peace, and extremists shot Sadat dead in 1981.
children.gloss: Furious Arab states boycotted Cairo for a separate peace, and extremists shot Sadat dead in 1981.

children.label: Palestinian Autonomy Left Unfulfilled
children.detail: Without PLO involvement, self-rule talks collapsed while Israeli settlements grew in the West Bank.
children.gloss: Without PLO involvement, self-rule talks collapsed while Israeli settlements grew in the West Bank.

children.label: Ended Multi-Front Arab War Threat
children.detail: Making peace with the strongest Arab army secured Israel's south and proved Land for Peace worked.
children.gloss: Making peace with the strongest Arab army secured Israel's south and proved Land for Peace worked.

children.label: 3.2 The Palestinian Issue
children.q2Chain: Arafat's 1974 UN speech, PLO raids in Lebanon & 1978 Operation Litani → 1982 Lebanon invasion, Beirut evacuation to Tunis & Sabra and Shatila → 1987–93 First Intifada in the occupied territories & rise of Hamas
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Arafat's 1974 UN speech, PLO raids in Lebanon & 1978 Operation Litani → 1982 Lebanon invasion, Beirut evacuation to Tunis & Sabra and Shatila → 1987–93 First Intifada in the occupied territories & rise of Hamas.

children.label: Arafat's UN Speech & Lebanon
children.gloss: Arafat's speech to the UN (1974) won official observer status while PLO activities in Lebanon turned southern 'Fatahland' into a cross-border base.

children.label: 1974 'Olive Branch & Gun' UN Speech
children.detail: Backed by Arab states, Arafat told the General Assembly Palestinians sought diplomacy or armed fight.
children.gloss: Backed by Arab states, Arafat told the General Assembly Palestinians sought diplomacy or armed fight.

children.label: PLO Built Bases in Southern Lebanon
children.detail: Fighters expelled from Jordan launched rockets and coastal raids into northern Galilee communities.
children.gloss: Fighters expelled from Jordan launched rockets and coastal raids into northern Galilee communities.

children.label: PLO Won Official UN Observer Status
children.detail: Over 100 nations recognised Palestinian self-determination even though Israel and America shunned it.
children.gloss: Over 100 nations recognised Palestinian self-determination even though Israel and America shunned it.

children.label: Fuelled 1975 Lebanese Civil War
children.detail: Armed Palestinian camps upset Lebanon's Christian-Muslim balance, igniting bitter sectarian fighting.
children.gloss: Armed Palestinian camps upset Lebanon's Christian-Muslim balance, igniting bitter sectarian fighting.

children.label: Reframed Palestinians as a Nation
children.detail: Global diplomacy moved beyond 242's refugee label, yet Lebanon attacks provoked major IDF reprisals.
children.gloss: Global diplomacy moved beyond 242's refugee label, yet Lebanon attacks provoked major IDF reprisals.

children.label: Israeli Reprisals (1978 Litani)
children.gloss: Ongoing PLO attacks from southern Lebanon provoked major Israeli reprisals, culminating in March 1978 Operation Litani and UNIFIL deployment.

children.label: Coastal Road Bus Attack (Mar 1978)
children.detail: Fatah militants landed from Lebanon and hijacked buses near Tel Aviv, killing 38 Israeli civilians.
children.gloss: Fatah militants landed from Lebanon and hijacked buses near Tel Aviv, killing 38 Israeli civilians.

children.label: Operation Litani Swept South Lebanon
children.detail: 25,000 Israeli soldiers pushed up to the Litani River for a week to clear frontline guerrilla camps.
children.gloss: 25,000 Israeli soldiers pushed up to the Litani River for a week to clear frontline guerrilla camps.

children.label: UNIFIL Peacekeepers Deployed
children.detail: Pressured by Carter during Camp David talks, Israel pulled out behind a new UN peacekeeping buffer.
children.gloss: Pressured by Carter during Camp David talks, Israel pulled out behind a new UN peacekeeping buffer.

children.label: PLO Fighters Returned & Fired Rockets
children.detail: Most guerrillas retreated north intact and soon resumed shelling Galilee towns across the border.
children.gloss: Most guerrillas retreated north intact and soon resumed shelling Galilee towns across the border.

children.label: Proved Limited Reprisals Failed
children.detail: Failing to uproot Arafat's border bases convinced Begin and Sharon to invade all the way to Beirut.
children.gloss: Failing to uproot Arafat's border bases convinced Begin and Sharon to invade all the way to Beirut.

children.label: 1982 Lebanon Invasion & Results
children.gloss: The invasion of Lebanon (1982) and its results expelled the PLO to Tunis, led to the Sabra and Shatila massacres, and spawned Hezbollah.

children.label: Argov Shooting → Op. Peace for Galilee
children.detail: After Israel's London ambassador was shot, Sharon pushed past 40km and besieged West Beirut for 10 weeks.
children.gloss: After Israel's London ambassador was shot, Sharon pushed past 40km and besieged West Beirut for 10 weeks.

children.label: PLO Expelled from Lebanon to Tunis
children.detail: 14,000 PLO fighters evacuated by sea under US escort, costing Arafat his last border base next to Israel.
children.gloss: 14,000 PLO fighters evacuated by sea under US escort, costing Arafat his last border base next to Israel.

children.label: Sabra & Shatila → Sharon Sacked
children.detail: Christian Phalangist allies killed hundreds in IDF-ringed camps, and Israel's Kahan Inquiry forced Sharon out.
children.gloss: Christian Phalangist allies killed hundreds in IDF-ringed camps, and Israel's Kahan Inquiry forced Sharon out.

children.label: Rise of Hezbollah in South Lebanon
children.detail: Iran-backed Shia militia emerged to fight Israeli troops occupying a costly southern security zone.
children.gloss: Iran-backed Shia militia emerged to fight Israeli troops occupying a costly southern security zone.

children.label: Strained US Ties & Pushed PLO to Talks
children.detail: Heavy Beirut civilian deaths shocked Washington, while distant Tunis exile nudged Arafat toward diplomacy.
children.gloss: Heavy Beirut civilian deaths shocked Washington, while distant Tunis exile nudged Arafat toward diplomacy.

children.label: Occupied Lands & First Intifada
children.gloss: Twenty years of rule in the Israeli occupied territories ignited the grassroots First Palestinian Intifada (1987–93), damaging Israel’s image and spawning Hamas.

children.label: 20 Years of Harsh Military Occupation
children.detail: Expanding settlements, curfews, and a December 1987 Gaza army lorry crash sparked mass uprising.
children.gloss: Expanding settlements, curfews, and a December 1987 Gaza army lorry crash sparked mass uprising.

children.label: Grassroots Strikes & Stone-Throwing
children.detail: Local Palestinian committees led tax boycotts, shop strikes, and youths confronting IDF patrols.
children.gloss: Local Palestinian committees led tax boycotts, shop strikes, and youths confronting IDF patrols.

children.label: Rabin's 'Iron Fist' Damaged Image
children.detail: Televised beatings, curfews, and mass arrests drew global criticism and divided Israeli opinion.
children.gloss: Televised beatings, curfews, and mass arrests drew global criticism and divided Israeli opinion.

children.label: Hamas Founded in Gaza (Dec 1987)
children.detail: Sheikh Yassin's Islamist movement vowed armed struggle for all Palestine, rivalling the secular PLO.
children.gloss: Sheikh Yassin's Islamist movement vowed armed struggle for all Palestine, rivalling the secular PLO.

children.label: Showed Force Alone Could Not Rule
children.detail: King Hussein dropped Jordan's West Bank claim in 1988, convincing Rabin only talks could bring calm.
children.gloss: King Hussein dropped Jordan's West Bank claim in 1988, convincing Rabin only talks could bring calm.

children.label: 3.3 Attempts at a Solution
children.q2Chain: Arafat's 1988 UN renunciation of terrorism, Cold War end & 1991 Gulf War / Madrid → Secret Norway talks, 1993 Oslo I Accord & 1994 PNA → 1994 Jordan treaty, 1995 Oslo II & Rabin's assassination
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Arafat's 1988 UN renunciation of terrorism, Cold War end & 1991 Gulf War / Madrid → Secret Norway talks, 1993 Oslo I Accord & 1994 PNA → 1994 Jordan treaty, 1995 Oslo II & Rabin's assassination.

children.label: Arafat Renounces Terror at UN
children.gloss: Arafat's renunciation of terrorism in a speech at the UN in December 1988 and acceptance of Resolution 242 ended the 13-year US diplomatic boycott.

children.label: Pressure From Intifada & Rival Hamas
children.detail: Exiled in Tunis after Jordan quit the West Bank, Arafat endorsed a two-state deal to stay relevant.
children.gloss: Exiled in Tunis after Jordan quit the West Bank, Arafat endorsed a two-state deal to stay relevant.

children.label: Dec 1988 UN Speech in Geneva
children.detail: Arafat explicitly renounced terrorism in all forms and accepted Israel's right to live under 242.
children.gloss: Arafat explicitly renounced terrorism in all forms and accepted Israel's right to live under 242.

children.label: USA Ended 13-Year PLO Boycott
children.detail: Meeting Kissinger's 1975 conditions persuaded Washington to open official diplomatic talks in Tunis.
children.gloss: Meeting Kissinger's 1975 conditions persuaded Washington to open official diplomatic talks in Tunis.

children.label: Likud & Militants Rejected Shift
children.detail: Israeli PM Shamir dismissed the pledge as a trick while Hamas condemned compromising over territory.
children.gloss: Israeli PM Shamir dismissed the pledge as a trick while Hamas condemned compromising over territory.

children.label: Unlocked Path to 1993 Oslo Talks
children.detail: Accepting Israel's existence removed the diplomatic barrier so Labour leaders could later negotiate.
children.gloss: Accepting Israel's existence removed the diplomatic barrier so Labour leaders could later negotiate.

children.label: Gulf War (1991) & Cold War End
children.gloss: Changing superpower policies in the Middle East through US involvement in the Gulf War (1991) and the end of the Cold War enabled the 1991 Madrid Conference.

children.label: Soviet Collapse Ended Arab Patronage
children.detail: Losing cheap Moscow arms and UN vetoes left the USA as the sole superpower shaping regional peace.
children.gloss: Losing cheap Moscow arms and UN vetoes left the USA as the sole superpower shaping regional peace.

children.label: Arafat Backed Saddam in 1991 Gulf War
children.detail: While a US-Arab coalition freed Kuwait and restrained Israel, PLO support for Iraq outraged Gulf states.
children.gloss: While a US-Arab coalition freed Kuwait and restrained Israel, PLO support for Iraq outraged Gulf states.

children.label: Gulf States Cut Off PLO Funding
children.detail: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait froze subsidies and expelled workers, pushing Arafat near bankruptcy.
children.gloss: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait froze subsidies and expelled workers, pushing Arafat near bankruptcy.

children.label: Madrid Peace Conference (Oct 1991)
children.detail: Using loan pressure, Washington brought Israel face-to-face with Syrian, Jordanian, and Palestinian envoys.
children.gloss: Using loan pressure, Washington brought Israel face-to-face with Syrian, Jordanian, and Palestinian envoys.

children.label: Weakened PLO & Boosted US Diplomacy
children.detail: Financial ruin and unrivalled American clout pushed Arafat toward major compromises in secret talks.
children.gloss: Financial ruin and unrivalled American clout pushed Arafat toward major compromises in secret talks.

children.label: Oslo Accords (1993) & PNA
children.gloss: Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat signed the Oslo Accords (1993) after secret Norway talks, achieving mutual recognition and founding the Palestinian National Authority.

children.label: 1992 Labour Win & Secret Oslo Talks
children.detail: Elected promising peace, Rabin approved quiet backchannel talks in Oslo, Norway away from the media.
children.gloss: Elected promising peace, Rabin approved quiet backchannel talks in Oslo, Norway away from the media.

children.label: Sept 1993 White House Lawn Handshake
children.detail: Before President Clinton, Israel and the PLO signed mutual recognition letters and interim accords.
children.gloss: Before President Clinton, Israel and the PLO signed mutual recognition letters and interim accords.

children.label: PNA Self-Rule in Gaza & Jericho (1994)
children.detail: IDF troops pulled back as Arafat returned from 27 years of exile to lead civil administration and police.
children.gloss: IDF troops pulled back as Arafat returned from 27 years of exile to lead civil administration and police.

children.label: Final-Status Flashpoints Postponed
children.detail: Leaving Jerusalem, refugees, borders, and settlements for five years let extremists attack trust.
children.gloss: Leaving Jerusalem, refugees, borders, and settlements for five years let extremists attack trust.

children.label: First Direct Israeli-Palestinian Deal
children.detail: Ending decades of mutual denial created self-governing institutions and cleared Jordan to sign peace.
children.gloss: Ending decades of mutual denial created self-governing institutions and cleared Jordan to sign peace.

children.label: Jordan Treaty (1994) & Oslo II
children.gloss: Oslo unlocked the Israel-Jordan peace treaty (1994) and Oslo II (1995), before extremist violence and Rabin’s assassination stalled peace.

children.label: Oct 1994 Israel-Jordan Peace Treaty
children.detail: Freed by the PLO deal, King Hussein and Rabin settled borders, shared river water, and opened trade.
children.gloss: Freed by the PLO deal, King Hussein and Rabin settled borders, shared river water, and opened trade.

children.label: Sept 1995 Oslo II: Areas A, B & C
children.detail: Expanded PNA self-rule to West Bank towns (Area A) while Israel kept 60% in Area C.
children.gloss: Expanded PNA self-rule to West Bank towns (Area A) while Israel kept 60% in Area C.

children.label: Settler Attack & Hamas Bus Bombings
children.detail: A Hebron mosque shooting and deadly Hamas suicide attacks in Israeli cities eroded public confidence.
children.gloss: A Hebron mosque shooting and deadly Hamas suicide attacks in Israeli cities eroded public confidence.

children.label: PM Yitzhak Rabin Assassinated (1995)
children.detail: Opposing West Bank handovers, Jewish extremist Yigal Amir shot Rabin dead after a Tel Aviv peace rally.
children.gloss: Opposing West Bank handovers, Jewish extremist Yigal Amir shot Rabin dead after a Tel Aviv peace rally.

children.label: Secured Jordan Yet Left Oslo Fragile
children.detail: By late 1995 two Arab neighbours were at peace with Israel, but terror and Rabin's murder stalled Oslo.
children.gloss: By late 1995 two Arab neighbours were at peace with Israel, but terror and Rabin's murder stalled Oslo.
